chapter: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
title: North African friends and police roundups during the Algerian War
summary: Butler befriended Tunisian Arabs among his customers, signalled them with The Bugle Blues when police vans closed in, and hid a man in the club.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: So now, musicwise, that was it. Now I'm getting involved with the Tunisian Arabs, and like one cat was spitting on the car (inaudible). And (inaudible) say, "He was spitting on your car. What should we do to him?" I said, "Take him down there and make him wash it off, and then give him some wine and let him come back in here and wash my car, watch it every now and then." "Okay, I got it. (Unintelligible)"

Then I got involved with a fellow I heard, he became the foreign minister of Tunisia. Well, I'd seen the man all the time. I said, I know (inaudible). And the police were running all the North Africans after them. They were after them. But they were part of (inaudible) where I was playing. And I'd see them park at a certain time. And I would play "The Bugle

'Blues'. And that would be a signal for them (inaudible). But their system is to have that black truck. It moves about ten feet all the time. Everybody forgets he's there. And before you know it, it is right there where you forget it. And then there's another one, he's a little bit further out there. And there's one there (inaudible). And all of a sudden, whack, got everybody.
Got everybody. And there's some new (inaudible).
Once they get in positions, everybody's gone.
So this was when the Algerian War was going on, they were rounding up all the Arabs?

Yes, man. So this cat, I said -- he was in it, I said (inaudible). And he went back there/and then and hid, the policemen, they didn't come in because they didn't have no reason to come in. I knew all the policemen, anyway. So all me. right, everything was cool, and he said, "Come with me said, 'You know, we're fighting for our freedom.' And he was going to school. And he became the foreign minister.
